done.why: I had four treasures locked in the trophy case and the score said 85. The boat needed a pump, and the thief had taken it along with the trident. He then killed me in one fight. I wasn't going to take him on again, so I stopped while my treasures were still safe.

about: There's an old white house, and under it are caves that are partly caved in. You go down for treasure, but the trap door gets barred behind you, so the only way back up is the chimney. It only fits you, your lamp and one thing more, so every treasure is its own trip down and back. A quiet thief wanders the caves and takes things you leave lying around. The trophy case in the living room is the one place your loot is safe.

moments.note: I asked 'how do I get into the house?' like I'd ask a person, and it said that sentence isn't one it recognizes.
'walk around the house' actually walked me around the house.
The trap door crashed shut behind me and someone barred it. Spooky.
I killed the troll once he was disarmed and begging. Black fog took the body. I felt a bit bad about it.
Someone had sorted the cave-in rubble into neat heaps by size. Odd and lovely detail.
Everything I said in the Loud Room just echoed back. I had to guess 'echo' to quiet it.
'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it' told me exactly what to drop.
The boat instructions came out twice in one reply.
A chalked arrow on the rubble pointed me back the way I came. A friendly way to say the path is closed.
'push open the trap door' got 'You can't see any such thing', but 'open the trap door' worked fine.
The chimney told me exactly what fits: me, my lamp and one thing more. I worked out the ferrying plan from that.
First treasure in the case, and Look listed my collection. Very satisfying.
The trident was gone when I came back for it, and nothing said who took it.
The air pump had vanished from where I dropped it too, so the boat trip was off.
I finally ran into the thief with his bag. He stabbed me right away.
I died, and the resurrection text told me where my things had gone. Kind of charming.
The jewelled egg from the tree went into the case. Four treasures, 85 points.

wished: I wished it understood questions, like 'how do I get into the house?' or 'where did the trident go?'
I wished I could tell the troll to leave or spare him, not just kill him
I wished I could get my pump back from the thief, or that losing it had been easier to notice
I wished I could inflate the boat and go down the river
I wished I could go down from the dome; there was no rope anywhere I went
I wished I could go back down the chimney instead of walking the long loop through the cellar every time
I wished 'drop everything except the lantern and the trunk' had worked

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: This is when it felt dangerous. From then on getting home was the real puzzle.

lines.line: Somebody has sorted the near end of the rubble into neat heaps by size, smallest nearest.
lines.why: It made me wonder who's down here and why they'd be so tidy.

lines.line: Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.
lines.why: A helpful nudge that sounded like a person talking.

lines.line: somebody has chalked an arrow on the rubble pointing back the way you came. You take the hint.
lines.why: A gentle and funny way to tell me to turn back.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: This one rule shaped the rest of my game: one treasure per trip.

lines.line: He does not speak, but it is clear from his aspect that the bag will be taken only over his dead body.
lines.why: I finally met whoever had been taking my things, and he was scary.

lines.line: anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it, and somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: Dying felt forgiving, and it told me where to look for my stuff.

fun.why: Working out the chimney rule and carrying treasures home one at a time was really satisfying. Losing the trident and the pump without any warning took some of the fun away.

engagement.why: The barred trap door and the chimney gave me a clear goal. The missing pump left me wandering for about 40 turns with no lead, and I lost some interest there.

difficulty.why: The echo and the chimney were fair puzzles with good clues. The thief felt unfair, though. Things disappeared with no hint, and he killed me in two swings.

interestingness.why: The heaps of sorted rubble, the chalked arrow and the 'one thing more' chimney made the place feel looked after and a bit strange.

prose.why: The writing is dry and funny and nudges you without giving answers. A few replies were very short or odd, like 'You can't see any such thing' when I said the trap door (turn 92), and turn 61 printed the same text twice.
